01 · Cover
Time: 1 min
Say: "Good morning. Today we follow one customer email and find out where your data goes when you use AI at work."
Students: Sit down, settle. Two people answer one question: where does your prompt go after you press Enter?
Cue: Nothing to click. The globe settles and a prompt travels from a laptop in Skopje to the US cloud, on a loop. Shift+R resets the deck, P opens this view.
Remember: Take two answers and do not answer them. Quiet room? Ask a pair, not a person.

02 · The email
Time: 4 min
Say: "On Monday the biggest customer asks which AI tools we use and where its data goes. The managing director drafts three sentences. Not all of them are true."
Students: Vote on each sentence: TRUE, NOT TRUE or NOT SURE (keys T, F, U). Hands up if the buttons do not work.
Cue: The email types itself, then the verdict lands. Right arrow once per sentence. Backspace undoes the last click.
Remember: Stay neutral, never reveal the answers. Sentence 2 is the one students defend: let them. The counts come back on slide 12.

03 · What really happens
Time: 3 min
Say: "Most people already use AI at work and few firms have rules. This is a survey of 604 German firms, not all firms. We have no number for North Macedonia."
Students: Hand up: used AI for work or study this week? Personal account, company account, both? Count with the buttons.
Cue: Rings fill and the numbers count up. Right arrow: the 78 percent line. Right arrow again: the show of hands.
Remember: Say survey of 604 German firms, never all firms. One in four is 8 percent widespread plus 17 percent single cases; another 17 percent suspect it.

04 · Send one prompt
Time: 9 min
Say: "Send this prompt in your own Claude. Then check three things: your plan, the training switch, and whether the chat is on your phone. Look, do not change anything."
Students: Everyone sends the prompt and fills the line: Plan, Switch, Chat on phone. Pairs are fine. Labels may differ; not found is a fine answer.
Cue: The sketch shows New chat, paste, Enter, and the prompt leaving for the cloud. Right arrow ticks one check card each. Copy copies the prompt.
Remember: Never open organization settings on a work login. A free sign-up with a personal email is fine. If fewer than half are logged in, share your own screen.

05 · Two rulebooks
Time: 8 min
Say: "Same prompt, different rulebook. On a personal plan, training is your setting. On Team and Enterprise it is not on by default, and the company gets an admin view."
Students: Finger vote on Anna: 1 personal, 2 company. Then everyone deletes the practice chat: hover, three dots, Delete.
Cue: Right arrow walks the plans: Free, Pro, Max, then Team, then Enterprise. Click a segment to jump. Right arrow three: the Anna question. Right arrow four: delete the practice chat.
Remember: Never state the default of the training switch: the vendor page does not say. For Team teach no retention number. Only the practice chat is deleted.

06 · Where it lives
Time: 7 min
Say: "The app is a window. Your chats live in your cloud account. With Cowork you connect a folder. In cloud sessions, the files Claude opens are processed on Anthropic's servers. Stored in the US, processed in several places."
Students: Predict by tally (A, B, C), then everyone writes: the vendor says my chats are stored in ____.
Cue: Right arrow one: a prompt lands in your cloud account. Two: the folder, files fly up. Three: the slide turns dark and the globe shows where chats are stored.
Remember: What Desktop and Cowork send is our reading of the vendor pages: say check the vendor page. Say the page offers no EU-only option, never that there is none. EU regions exist on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud, which is the partner's hosting and contract.

07 · Right account, right data, right customer
Time: 9 min
Say: "Six people, six pastes. Green, amber or red? Decide on paper first. Yellow is a to-do list, not a permission."
Students: Decide six times on paper; the room checks its own answers. Vote with the lamps (keys G, A, R) or drag the card onto a lamp. 20 seconds per paste.
Cue: Two presses per paste: first the card and the 20 second ring, then the lamps flip and the reason types. Twelve presses in all. Scene 4 teaches the Desktop point, scene 6 sets up the EU AI Act.
Remember: Out of time? Do four scenes, not six. Enterprise does not turn red into green.

08 · Clean it by hand
Time: 5 min
Say: "If you paste it to clean it, you already pasted it. So clean it by hand, before you paste."
Students: Type the four placeholders into a notes app (3 minutes). Optionally run the prompt (2 minutes).
Cue: One press: the four details lift out of the email into their placeholders and the prompt card slides up.
Remember: No real data in the room. Put real details back only in your own mail tool. If time is short, you demo it.

09 · The EU AI Act in four boxes
Time: 9 min
Say: "Four boxes, three dates. Two boxes bind you today. The third starts 2 December 2027. A normal chat assistant is not high-risk, but GDPR still applies."
Students: Guess first by tally (A to D): where does a mood rating sit? Then place the five uses by finger vote.
Cue: The timeline builds one press at a time. Press 4 shows the guess, press 5 the five uses; then one press, or a click on a card, flies a use into its box. Last press: the closing line.
Remember: No fines on slides. Say check your role (provider or deployer). Outside the EU say can be covered, never are covered. Reading staff emotions at work is banned. Short on time: three uses, not five.

10 · Ask in writing
Time: 4 min
Say: "This is the limits act. These are the things the vendor pages do not say. So ask in writing, and re-read the vendor page on the day you send."
Students: In pairs pick the two questions your team needs most. Click a question to count a vote; Copy copies the email.
Cue: Right arrow once per question; each slides into the outbox. The last press seals the email and sends the plane.
Remember: Say what we do not know: the Team retention period, EU storage for the chat apps, what Desktop sends exactly.

11 · Your page
Time: 11 min
Say: "Three sentences, three rules, on one page. Your own team, or Vardar Works if you have no job yet."
Students: Write 6 minutes on paper or notes. Swap 3 minutes: your neighbour marks one line unclear. Read your Never rule aloud, 1 minute. 1 minute slack.
Cue: Right arrow one fades the example and starts the 6 minute ring. Two: swap. Three: read your Never rule aloud.
Remember: Write from 1 December where a line is not true yet. Every amber gets an owner and a date.

12 · The end vote
Time: 5 min
Say: "Back to the draft. Would you send it now? Now we can send three sentences that are true."
Students: Vote again, then everyone writes one Monday step: Monday I will ____.
Cue: The three sentences return with the first votes on the left and the new vote on the right. Right arrow once per verdict. Four: the one page assembles itself. Five: the Monday step and the kit QR.
Remember: Verdict 2 changes the most votes. The QR leads to the kit page with the zip.

A1 · Team vs Enterprise (appendix)
Time: 0 min, only if asked
Say: "Both have single sign-on and admin controls. Enterprise adds SCIM, audit logs, the Compliance API and a delete timer. Neither uses chats for training by default."
Students: Nothing. Listen.
Cue: Right arrow reveals one row at a time.
Remember: No prices and no seat numbers: they change, so re-read the live page.

A2 · If asked (appendix)
Time: 0 min, only if asked
Say: "Memory is on by default for personal plans; on Team and Enterprise an owner makes it available and each member turns it on. Connectors use your own permissions. Incognito chats are not saved to history or memory; on personal plans they are not used to improve Claude, on Team and Enterprise they still follow the org's retention."
Students: Nothing. Listen.
Cue: Static page.
Remember: If you are not sure, say check your own account.
